tasks.summary: Reviewed all submitted changed segments, the pinned design, acceptance checks, and relevant test assertions. No blocking implementation defect found; two minor coverage gaps remain.

findings.message: The new-chat assertion exercises only an empty current provider.
findings.rationale: ac3 requires preserving the current provider. This test never sends a nonempty run-config provider and therefore does not behaviorally verify that requirement. The implementation and source assertion are correct; add a nonempty-provider case.

findings.message: The aggregate-status test does not assert that urgency survives selecting a differently ranked chat.
findings.rationale: ac4 explicitly requires this distinction. The test checks aggregate waiting-input before selecting working Chat B, then checks only open-chat. Assert that the chip remains waiting-input after selection and restoration. Static inspection shows the implementation preserves it.

Source assertions cover removal of provider repainting and markup/CSP compatibility. The two narrower behavioral assertion gaps are recorded as LOW findings. Browser smoke remains builder-reported evidence, not reviewer execution.

tasks.summary: Reviewed all submitted segments, the pinned LLD, all acceptance checks, and relevant test assertions. The implementation follows the design, but the new menus can overflow narrow viewports.

findings.message: The fixed 220px minimum width defeats the viewport width constraint.
findings.rationale: Below a 248px viewport width, min-width:220px overrides max-width:calc(100vw - 28px). For example, at 200px the active menu extends past the right edge, while the right-anchored history menu extends past the left edge and is clipped by the containing box. Constrain the minimum width by the available viewport width too. The reported smoke checks only a 1280px viewport.

findings.message: Some claimed acceptance behaviors lack behavioral assertions.
findings.rationale: The new-chat test asserts only provider:'' without delivering a nonempty run-config provider. Icon assertions cover Claude and Codex, but never Vibe; the helper's Vibe branch is unused. The status test asserts aggregate urgency before selecting a differently ranked row, without asserting its preservation afterward. Add these cases to substantiate the corresponding ac1/ac3/ac4 claims.

Browser smoke results are builder-reported; their JSON records outcomes without assertion bodies or a revision pin, so they do not independently establish browser behavior.
